### Axel ingress review 044: seats, terminal hold and service limits

At reviewed head `abcaef007828526bf7695057ddeba6bc4bc5173d`, `Room.players` is the stable seat vector for the attached runtime's lifetime. Attachment validates each room index against the Match slot/configuration (`lobby.rs:735-748`). Attached roster-changing commands are blocked (`:453-473`), a new token cannot append a seat (`:1443-1446`), and takeover changes the existing Person's connection/name/disconnected state without moving the Person (`:1430-1441`). Disconnect clears the connection in place (`:1521-1524`), and expiry skips seat compaction while attached (`:1568-1570`). Result finalization clears `native` before retaining/reindexing lobby seats (`:303-307`). Thus actual tick feedback at `:1251-1253` addresses the issuer's unchanged seat, including after takeover or reconnect. An entirely abandoned room may expire, ending that lifetime rather than reassigning its attached seats.

`held() >= 120` is terminal post-win handling, not a resumable pause. The private hold counter starts at zero and increments only when `Match.finish` exists; every second callback advances, and callback 120 completes (`room_runtime.rs:123`, `:362-374`). Resume clears only the pause, not the finish or counter (`:305-307`). The Hub's completing callback runs result finalization and detaches the runtime; a failure faults it (`lobby.rs:1228-1237`, `:268-307`). The terminal/fault branch drops feedback names and skips further stepping (`:1152-1154`); it cannot later resume that Match's queued commands. New player inputs after a decided finish are already blocked before key reservation (`commander_ingress.rs:41-42`). Previously accepted service inputs target only the next boundary (`:101-125`), whose queue dispatch precedes the winning step (`match_tick.rs:363-369`; `match_commands.rs:666-680`). Preloaded future host/replay keys have no service feedback names and do not acquire them. This is separate from drop-pause resume, which preserves the runtime and its queued inputs.

Whole-command `Unsupported` is a temporary limitation of this initial service slice, not the prototype's command semantics. After parsing, the capability scan skips missing/foreign and other source-ineligible IDs, then refuses the entire payload if any remaining row has AIR/naval metadata, a Move targets a garrisoned actor, Move/Stop targets an active builder, or AutoRetreat-on targets a garrisoned actor or builder (`commander_ingress.rs:51-98`). Other Stance commands are not blanket-refused merely because an actor is garrisoned or building. Refusal occurs before any input key, sequence or feedback-name publication (`:100-135`); it does not partially enqueue the supported rows. Unsupported malformed state may separately fail the existing whole-state guard.

The pinned prototype filters selected units through `mine`, then handles each valid movement request (`reference/ww2-rts/shared/sim.js:3419-3429`), including AIR patrol (`:3442`), building exit and job/intent clearing (`:3451-3452`). The service does not claim that behavior is fully connected. It preserves the supported rows' canonical core selection when the capability scan succeeds, while mixed eligible unsupported rows currently prevent the entire service command. Extending those actor contexts requires their actual actuator/caller proof; this documentation change weakens no guard and changes no runtime, test, wire or privacy rule.

## Native server diagnostics (2026-10-16)

NET-97 uses the existing host tick meter and an opt-in bounded writer. `WW2_DIAG=1` appends room JSONL records under the process working directory's `logs/`; `WW2_TICKLOG=1` prints phase percentiles every thirty seconds. Library hosts choose a diagnostic directory through `Config`. A 64-record channel keeps file writes outside the room lock; full queues and file errors discard diagnostic records without affecting the match. Native scheduler delay measures excess over the ten-millisecond maintenance poll, providing the equivalent of the prototype's event-loop delay. Timestamps are Unix milliseconds. A separate optional socket gauge measures queued UTF-8 payload bytes for all output classes and preserves the existing UTF-16 snapshot admission threshold. Browser metrics stay host-private. None of these measurements enters the deterministic rules state or recipient snapshots.

## Horde wave phase and scenario type validation (2026-10-16)

`Match::step_horde` is an explicit late phase after ordinary capture, income
and death removal. It does not advance the clock or run combat. Wave purchases,
reserve entry and clearing use canonical Match state; newly entered units act
on the following tick. Full Horde tick and server admission remain guarded.
Vehicle entry must pass the current World navigation and obstruction versions
to the persistent production placer, just as ordinary recruitment does, so
terrain changes invalidate cached clearance between entries.

Native scenario validation deliberately requires a JSON string for each authored
unit or reinforcement roster `type`. It rejects `type: ["rifle"]`, whereas the
prototype's `Object.hasOwn(unitTypes, v)` and `unitTypes[v]` coerce that array to
the property name `"rifle"`. This stricter choice rejects malformed schema values
instead of carrying JavaScript property-key coercion into the native validator.
It does not admit or execute general authored scenarios.

shopping. It finishes or repairs an existing building before searching for a
